articles.title: Kulgam terror attack : DG CRPF reviews security, LeT terrorist in crosshairs
articles.description: Meets field officers, discusses intensifying counter-insurgency ops Massive frisking, vehicle checks across Valley Srinagar, Nov 13: Director General (DG), Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Gyanendra Pratap Singh, on Friday visited south Kashmir's Kulgam district and reviewed the security situation amid an intensified manhunt for Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Mohammed Lateef Bhat, suspected to be involved in Wednesday's attack on CRPF personnel. Two days after three CRPF personnel were injured in the attack at Nowpora Akhran near Mir Bazar, Kulgam, the CRPF chief took stock of the security arrangements and interacted with field officers. He also met CRPF and Jammu and Kashmir Police officers at Sadura in neighbouring Anantnag district and discussed measures to intensify counter-insurgency operations in the Valley. A senior CRPF official said the visit was aimed at assessing the ground situation and reviewing security arrangements following the attack. "The force is maintaining heightened vigil and coordinating with other security agencies as efforts continue to track down those responsible," he said. Meanwhile, security has been significantly tightened across Kashmir, with massive frisking and checking operations being conducted in several districts, including Srinagar. Police and paramilitary personnel have intensified searches of vehicles, passengers and pedestrians at major intersections, market areas, highways and other vulnerable locations. In Srinagar, additional security personnel have been deployed at important junctions and entry and exit points, with vehicles being stopped for checking and commuters subjected to frisking and identity verification. CRPF officials said additional checkpoints have been established, while armoured vehicles and security personnel have been deployed at strategic points. "Security agencies are also maintaining heightened vigil along important roads and in areas considered vulnerable to terrorist activity," they said. The intensified measures come as the joint manhunt in Kulgam continues, with several search operations underway to track down the suspected attackers. Investigators suspect that LeT terrorist Mohammed Lateef Bhat was among the attackers after the injured CRPF personnel reportedly recognised his photograph. Bhat is also suspected of involvement in earlier attacks in south Kashmir, including the July assault on two migrant labourers in Kelam near Akhran village and the killing of a police head constable in Anantnag the same month. Police have reportedly described Bhat as the last surviving local terrorist active in the Valley and believe he is being supported by a few foreign terrorists. Security agencies are examining the possible support network and movement of the suspected attackers. The attack took place around 2:15 pm on November 11 when two to three suspected terrorists opened fire on a CRPF naka party near Akhran Bridge at Mir Bazar. Three personnel belonging to the CRPF's 46th Battalion sustained bullet injuries — Head Constable Somveer Singh and Constables Rakesh Dass and Santosh Chandru. One personnel sustained serious bullet injuries to the abdomen and spine and was shifted to the Army's 92 Base Hospital in Srinagar, while the other two suffered injuries to their limbs. The National Investigation Agency also visited the attack site to collect forensic evidence and examine material that could help reconstruct the sequence of events.

articles.title: Manipur: 4 Nagas killed in suspected Kuki militant ambush
articles.description: IMPHAL: Four Tangkhul Naga civilians, including two women, were killed after suspected Kuki militants opened fire on two vehicles along the Ukhrul–Imphal road (NH-202) at New Heaven in Ukhrul district on Friday, police said. The victims, comprising two men and two women, reportedly died on the spot. Bullet marks were found on the windshields of the vehicles. Two of the deceased were from Tashar village, while the other two—a mother and her son—were from Shangshak village. Read More: Manipur: Woman killed, 3 injured as Kuki militants attack Naga cultivators working in paddy fields New Heaven is located opposite Yaolen, a Kuki village where Assam Rifles personnel are deployed. Preliminary reports alleged that cadres of the Kuki National Front (KNF), Kuki National Army (KNA) and Kuki Liberation Army (KLA), allegedly backed by Myanmar-based KNA (Burma), were involved in the ambush. The attackers reportedly fled after the shooting. However, the alleged involvement of these groups has not been independently confirmed by police. The killings came a day after a Tangkhul Naga farmer, Newton Mahung (49), son of late Mayonmi Mahung, was shot and injured while harvesting paddy at Ihang Plains near Sinakeithel village on November 12. The incident also falls under Litan Police Station’s jurisdiction. Mahung reportedly sustained a gunshot injury while working in his field, around 300 metres from the village settlement. Read More: Manipur: COCOMI Seeks Rehabilitation for 2,000 Displaced Naga People, Calls for SoO Abrogation The back-to-back attacks have heightened concerns over civilian safety in Ukhrul district, particularly among farmers working in fields and people travelling along the Ukhrul–Imphal highway.

articles.title: Kulgam CRPF Attack | AK-47 Firing , 3 Injured | NIA Probe & Terrorist Manhunt | Jammu Kashmir
articles.description: A terror attack on a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) checkpoint in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district has triggered a security operation and an investigation by multiple agencies. The firing took place on Wednesday, November 11, around 2:15 pm at Akhran, near Mir Bazar, where CRPF personnel were deployed. Three jawans sustained bullet injuries, including one who was initially reported to be in critical condition. The latest reports say all three are stable. Preliminary inputs indicate that the attackers approached the checkpoint on foot and opened fire using AK-47 rifles. Investigators are examining CCTV footage and forensic evidence to establish the sequence of events and identify those involved. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) visited the attack site on November 12 to collect samples and assist with the forensic examination. The case remains under investigation by Jammu and Kashmir Police; it has not been formally transferred to the NIA. A preliminary investigation cited by a senior police officer points to the involvement of at least three terrorists, with two suspected to be foreign nationals. Other reports have cited different initial assessments of the number of attackers, and the investigation is continuing.
